newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso tries to keep Brazil re-election on track.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso tries to keep Brazil re-election on track.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, seeking to keep his plans for a second term on track, summoned the leaders of Brazil's biggest political party to a meeting on Monday to discuss its opposition to his re-election.

A presidential spokeswoman said Cardoso would meet with leaders of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), which on Sunday decided not to deal with the issue until Feb. 15, denting government hopes of quick approval of a re-election bid.

The decision, overriding the views of the PMDB's pro-government wing at a tumultuous party convention, threatened to derail a timetable for voting on a constitutional amendment that would allow re-election.

It was due to begin with a committee vote on the amendment on Tuesday but it was unclear if that could take place without the PMDB, which has six of the 30 members of the committee. A presidential spokeswoman said the meeting would take place but declined to comment on its likely outcome.

A government source in Congress said he expected the president would insist that voting take place on Tuesday as scheduled. "The government wants to show that it is willing to vote independently of what the PMDB thinks," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

Cardoso, seeking to become Brazil's first re-elected president, called a special session of Congress this month in an attempt to get re-election approved in the Chamber of Deputies. The government wanted the deputies to approve the amendment before Cardoso's loyal ally, Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes, steps down as president of the lower house in February.
But the PMBD, which is split between pro- and anti-goverment wings, insisted it would not vote on re-election until it had won the presidencies of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.
